0.name: Pre-diagnosis
0.description: - Patient goes for tests, and mammogram, Ultrasound, US and biopsy. It can be either of the following- Mammogram + Biopsy, or US + biopsy or MMG+US_Biopsy

1.1.name: palliative
1.1.description: Metastasis has happened and hence curative treatment is not possible.

1.2.name: primary endocrine
1.2.description: endocrine (anti hormone medication) as first line treatment. There are multiple reasons for choosing this treatment path, the most common one being patient may not be fit for surgery.

1.2.1.name: Follow-up Clinic
1.2.1.description: follow up to see if hormone treatment is working with a Specialist Clinician (this is not same as results clinic)

1.3.name: Further investigation
1.3.description: Following review of previous work up in the MDM, patient is reviewed in results clinic to discuss next step, which could be either to start treatment or for further investigation,

2.2.name: Axillary surgery
2.2.description: Surgery to assess or treat lymph nodes under the arm, helping guide breast cancer treatment decisions.
verification_questions: Is your surgery on armpit? or -
Option 1: Only a few lymph glands being removed (sentinel lymph node biopsy)
Option 2: All lymph glands being removed (Axillary lymph node clearance)

2.1.name: Breast surgery
2.1.description: Operations on the breast to remove cancer and, when possible, preserve appearance and function.

2.1.1.name: Breast Conservation Surgery
2.1.1.description: Operations which remove the cancer while keeping most of the breast, almost always followed by radiotherapy.
verification_questions: Is your surgery to remove the tumor only and not the whole breast? or -
Option 2: Remove tumor (Lumpectomy) and remove and reduce the breast (Therapeutic mammaplasty)
Option 3: Remove the tumor (Lumpectomy) and fill the defect with skin and fat from chest wall (Chest wall perforator flap)

2.1.2.name: Mastectomy
2.1.2.description: Operations which remove all the breast tissue, including the cancer.
verification_questions: Is your surgery to remove whole breast? or -
Option 2: Remove breast (Mastectomy) and reconstruction with implant
Option 3: Remove breast (Mastectomy) and reconstruction with own tissue (autologous)

2.2.2.name: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
2.2.2.description: Operation in which only the first 1-3 draining lymph nodes are removed to check for cancer spread.

2.2.3.name: Axillary Lymph node clearance
2.2.3.description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments. This is done when there is confirmed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.

3.3.name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with targeted therapy
3.3.description: Chemotherapy combined with drugs targeting specific cancer features or pathways, before surgery, improving response to chemotherapy and reducing recurrence risk, usually used in specific breast cancer type (e.g. blocking growth factor receptors in HER2 +ve cancer)

3.1.name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy
3.1.description: Anti-cancer drugs given before surgery to kill cancer cells

3.2.name: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with immunotherapy
3.2.description: Chemotherapy combined with immune-boosting treatment, before surgery, to help your body attack cancer cells, usually used in specific breast cancer type (called triple negative cancer).

4.4.name: Neoadjuvant endocrine treatment
4.4.description: Hormone-blocking treatment, given before surgery, to slow growth of cancer if you are temporarily unfit for surgery, or to shrink the cancer if you are unfit for traditional chemotherapy. This can only be used in hormone-sensitive breast cancer.

5.5.name: Survivorship
5.5.description: Patient has completed active treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy) and is now in the survivorship phase. Regular follow-up appointments will continue to monitor for recurrence.

5.1.name: No medication
5.1.description: Patient has completed all treatment and does not require ongoing medication. Regular monitoring and follow-up appointments continue.

5.2.name: Endocrine treatment and/or Zometa
5.2.description: Patient continues on endocrine therapy (hormone tablets) and/or zoledronic acid (Zometa) as part of long-term treatment to reduce recurrence risk.

6.6.name: Further surgery
6.6.description: After pathology review of the first surgery, further surgery may be needed if there is suspicion of residual cancer in the breast or in the lymph nodes.
verification_questions: Do you need further surgery after your first surgery?

6.1.name: Axilla lymph node clearance
6.1.description: Operation in which "all" underarm lymph nodes are removed to treat known cancer spread, and assess cancer burden to plan further treatments. This is done when there is confirmed cancer spread in the lymph nodes.
verification_questions: Do you need further surgery to remove all lymph nodes (Axillary lymph nodes clearance)

6.2.name: Breast margin excision
6.2.description: Operation in which breast tissue (suspected to contain residual cancer) is removed.
verification_questions: Do you need further surgery to remove more breast tissue?

6.3.name: Completion mastectomy
6.3.description: Operation in which all breast tissue is removed, as it is suspected to contain residual cancer.

7.7.name: Adjuvant radiotherapy
7.7.description: Treatment with radiation to the breast (after breast conservation surgery), or to chest wall (after mastectomy, advanced cancer), or to other nodal areas (like supraclavicular or internal mammary areas)

8.8.name: Adjuvant chemotherapy
8.8.description: Systemic administration of medications to kill cancer cells. Chemotherapy may be combined with immunotherapy (for triple negative cancer), or targeted therapy (in HER2 positive cancer), or with zoledronic acid (for women with high risk breast cancer, to reduce risk of bone recurrence).

9.9.name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy
9.9.description: Endocrine therapy is indicated in patients with estrogen receptor positive breast cancer. This is typically the last leg of treatment.
verification_questions: Option 2: Hormone Therapy and Zoledronic Acid

9.1.name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy only
9.1.description: Endocrine therapy is indicated in patients with estrogen receptor positive breast cancer.

9.2.name: Adjuvant endocrine therapy and Zoledronic acid
9.2.description: In postmenopausal women, zoledronic acid is indicated in combination with endocrine therapy to improve survival by inhibiting bone breakdown.

10.name: Adjuvant Zoledronic acid (Zometa)
10.description: In postmenopausal women, zoledronic acid is indicated to improve survival by inhibiting bone breakdown. Often given in combination with endocrine therapy.
